evidence_semantics: The primary anti-CD70 Ab-MCC-DM1 study used lysosome enrichment and mass spectrometry and states that catabolism to Lys-MCC-DM1 occurs in the lysosomal compartment; earlier cellular work and later T-DM1 work independently identify the same major catabolite.
allowed_claim: A true amino-acid-linker-payload catabolite of noncleavable MCC/SMCC-DM1 ADCs can be used as a release-catabolite demonstration object.
prohibited_claim: It is not free DM1 and the retained single PubChem stereoisomer must not be presented as a literal representation of the registered epimeric mixture.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Human MDR1-LLC-PK1 bidirectional experiment was interpreted by the source as low P-gp potential; figure-level values remain a separate curation task.

evidence_semantics: Kovtun et al. exposed COLO 205MDR cells to anti-EpCAM-PEG4Mal-[3H]DM1; the intracellular HPLC peak matched synthetic Lys-PEG4Mal-DM1 and the identity was confirmed by electrospray mass spectrometry.
allowed_claim: The named Lys-PEG4Mal-DM1 catabolite is experimentally supported for the specified experimental ADC.
prohibited_claim: A chemical drawing without an independently curated identifier or machine-readable structure is insufficient for molecular scoring; it must not be counted as a scored structure.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Relative retention in MDR1-expressing cells is not a direct transporter truth label.

evidence_semantics: Erickson et al. identified Lys-SPDB-DM4 after cellular processing of huC242-SPDB-DM4 and placed it upstream of disulfide reduction and S-methylation; the exact small-molecule structure is cross-registered as DM4-SPDB-L-lysine.
allowed_claim: It is a directly observed Lys-linker-payload processing product and may be shown as an intermediate application object.
prohibited_claim: It is not the terminal membrane-permeable DM4 species and its behavior must not be transferred to free DM4 or S-methyl-DM4.
abcb1_evidence_summary: No endpoint-aligned exact-entity ABCB1 truth was used.

release_stage: downstream metabolite after DM4 release and S-methylation
evidence_semantics: Cellular processing work identified S-methyl-DM4 downstream of Lys-SPDB-DM4; the EMA Elahere assessment additionally reports formation from DM4 and measured human plasma exposure after mirvetuximab soravtansine.
allowed_claim: It is an experimentally supported active downstream ADC-derived metabolite.
prohibited_claim: It is not bare DM4 and should not be called the initial lysosomal cleavage product.
abcb1_evidence_summary: A regulatory review calls S-methyl-DM4 a P-gp substrate but does not reproduce numeric transport data.

evidence_semantics: Primary liver-metabolism work supports reduction and S-methylation in the mAb-SPP-DM1 pathway, and the DDI paper treats S-methyl-DM1 as a representative cleavable-linker catabolite; however, the review notes that S-methyl-DM1 is not readily observed as a tumor-cell catabolite and the current row is not closed to one named ADC plus direct exact-species measurement.
allowed_claim: It may be retained as a supportive ADC-related modified-payload metabolite.
prohibited_claim: It must not be described as a directly confirmed major terminal release product of a specific named ADC, and the PubChem record with unspecified stereochemistry is not an exact stereochemical material identity.
abcb1_evidence_summary: MDR1-associated cytotoxicity shifts support susceptibility but are not bidirectional flux measurements.

evidence_semantics: The PMDA assessment explicitly identifies cys-mcMMAF as the small molecule released from belantamab mafodotin after antibody proteolysis and reports LC-MS/MS measurements in plasma and tissues; Durbin et al. independently quantified released cys-mcMMAF from a noncleavable experimental ADC by LC-MS/MS.
allowed_claim: It is a true cysteine-linker-payload catabolite and an active released species for the named ADC context.
prohibited_claim: It is not free MMAF; the conflicting PubChem preferred-title/whole-ADC synonyms should not be used as evidence that the whole ADC and catabolite are the same entity.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Human P-gp-MDCK ER was 34 and fell to 1.1 with verapamil in the regulatory summary.

evidence_semantics: Durbin et al. quantified unconjugated MMAE released from the cleavable Ab033-vcMMAE construct in cells by LC-MS/MS against authentic standards.
allowed_claim: Bare MMAE is a directly measured terminal release product for the specified cleavable experimental ADC.
prohibited_claim: The observation must not be generalized to every MMAE ADC because linker chemistry and processing can instead yield residual-linker products.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Independent Caco-2 and MDR1-MDCK studies report high ER with inhibitor rescue.

evidence_semantics: Caculitan et al. measured cys-VC-MMAE in cell lysate and medium by mass spectrometry and showed that the noncleavable VC(R) construct did not release free MMAE; the PMDA polatuzumab dossier separately identifies cys-vc-MMAE in rat bile with the expected mass and structure.
allowed_claim: It is a directly observed linker-bearing processing product suitable for a mechanistic-intermediate demonstration.
prohibited_claim: It is neither bare MMAE nor a universal terminal product of vc-MMAE ADCs; the source-specific S/R linker context must remain visible.
abcb1_evidence_summary: No exact-entity endpoint-aligned ABCB1 truth was used.

evidence_semantics: A stable-isotope LC-HRMS study measured free SN-38, total SN-38 and SN-38G after sacituzumab govitecan in a xenograft model; the primary mechanistic study and FDA review support release of SN-38 through CL2A hydrolysis.
allowed_claim: Bare SN-38 is an analytically supported actual released payload of sacituzumab govitecan.
prohibited_claim: The result does not establish that all SN-38 ADCs have the same release location or kinetics and does not make SN-38G an initial active release product.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Caco-2 experiments support P-gp involvement, but the system is not single-gene isolated.

evidence_semantics: The intratumor-fate study reports pH-dependent cysteine-protease release of DXd in lysosomal fractions; the FDA chemistry review explicitly crosswalks MAAA-1181a to DXd, and the original DS-8201a study describes release of the same hydroxyl-containing DXd species by the GGFG self-immolative system.
allowed_claim: Bare DXd/MAAA-1181a is a confirmed actual released payload of trastuzumab deruxtecan.
prohibited_claim: Deruxtecan linker-payload must not be substituted for DXd, and evidence for one DXd ADC does not automatically identify the release species of every DXd-platform construct.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Regulatory substrate calls and Caco-2 inhibitor-attributed ER are directionally positive but heterogeneous.

release_evidence_method: ADC design and matched payload activity
evidence_semantics: A later OBI-992 primary study quantified free exatecan by LC-MS/MS after OBI-992 incubation and dosing, including serum and tumor exposure; a 2026 validated human bioanalytical study also quantified systemic unconjugated exatecan after OBI-992. These sources upgrade the earlier design-only assignment.
allowed_claim: Exatecan is an analytically confirmed systemic unconjugated payload after OBI-992 dosing and may be included as an actual unconjugated-payload object.
prohibited_claim: The evidence does not establish intracellular release location and must not be described as confirmed intracellular release; it also does not establish identical release kinetics across all exatecan ADCs.
abcb1_evidence_summary: Caco-2 results are low or source-called non-substrate in one study; no clean universal binary truth is assigned.

residual_group: physicochemical modifier retained after legumain cleavage
release_evidence_method: ADC design, biological activity and author naming
evidence_semantics: The BAY-943 primary paper explicitly calls BAY-716 the active toxophore metabolite released intracellularly from the legumain-cleavable ADC and reports its permeability, but no direct catabolite-identification experiment is shown; the chemistry paper depicts an active metabolite structure without explicitly mapping compound 8 to the code BAY-716.
allowed_claim: BAY-716 may be retained as an author-named active metabolite of BAY-943.
prohibited_claim: No molecular structure may be assigned by inference from compound 8 and it must not be scored until an explicit name-to-structure crosswalk is recovered.
abcb1_evidence_summary: The source reports ER 1.6, but the exact structure crosswalk is unresolved and the system is not gene isolated.

evidence_semantics: The primary pharmacology paper explicitly defines SG3199 as the released warhead component of tesirine; the FDA loncastuximab review and the tesirine chemistry literature independently use the same SG3199 identity, although the cited pharmacology paper does not itself quantify post-ADC release by LC-MS.
allowed_claim: SG3199 is an exact free warhead and may be used as an explicitly assigned released-payload object for tesirine ADCs.
prohibited_claim: It should not be upgraded to direct analytical release grade unless a named ADC study measuring generated SG3199 is cited.
abcb1_evidence_summary: FDA P-gp substrate call and MDR1-transfectant functional resistance are directionally concordant; neither is a reproduced direct-flux dataset here.
